subject: Dedicated capacity surge — interim mitigation & next-step commitments
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity surge — interim mitigation & next-step commitments

Hi Elena,

I wanted to reach out directly with an immediate update and a clear set of next steps following the capacity surge BrightRetail experienced this morning (we saw elevated 429s and latency spikes across your Dedicated pool between ~08:45–09:05 PST). First, I’m very sorry for the disruption — we understand this impacted customer-facing experiences for your recommendations service.

What we have done so far (interim):
- Kept a warm spare of your reserved nodes online and moved ~30% of traffic off the saturated pool by 08:58.
- Temporarily lowered autoscaler aggressiveness for your tenant to reduce oscillation while we investigate.
- Enabled fallback routing to the smaller model variant for non-critical requests to maintain headroom.

What we’re committing to next:
1) Full RCA and timeline within 72 hours (target: Mon 2026-11-09 09:00 PST).
2) A remediation package that includes an autoscaler config hardening, an additional warm standby for peak windows, and a telemetry dashboard for BrightRetail-specific headroom alerts.
3) A goodwill credit for the impacted period; we’ll propose options after the RCA.

I’ve cc’d Ben (ops lead) and Aditya (runtime) so you have direct engineering touchpoints. Please let me know if you want a short sync in the next hour — otherwise we’ll send a follow-up with a detailed timeline and the interim mitigation plan attached.

Kimberly Park
Account Lead, Enterprise Success
Redwood Inference

Team — quick internal note after the sync with BrightRetail at 10:15:

Summary from ops/engineering:
- Observed: Dedicated allocator entered a saturation loop when a combination of short-burst traffic and KV-cache warmup caused queue depth to spike. Autoscaler threshold was tuned to favor rapid scale-down and didn’t pre-warm additional nodes for short bursts.
- Immediate fix applied: disabled aggressive scale-down for BrightRetail and bumped warm-standby count by 1 node.
- Short-term follow-ups (this week):
  * Change autoscaler hysteresis for dedicated pools (Aditya) — prevention of flapping on sub-minute bursts.
  * Add per-tenant headroom alerts tied to queue depth and prefix-KV miss rates (Ben/Laura).
  * Run a controlled load replay against BrightRetail config to validate fixes (ops).

External comms: Kimberly to send a concise customer-facing timeline and propose two credit options: (A) flat credit equal to 15% of the impacted week’s Dedicated invoice, or (B) 50% credit on the token overage attributable to the incident window.

Ben
Senior Technical Program Manager, Customer Ops

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident update: findings, timeline, and proposed credit options (BrightRetail)

Hi Elena — thanks again for your patience while we completed the initial investigation. Below is a concise post-incident summary, a timeline of actions, and two credit options for your review. I’ll also schedule a 30-minute wrap-up with the engineering team if you’d like to go deeper.

Executive summary:
- Root cause: An autoscaler hysteresis misconfiguration for tenant-level dedicated pools combined with a KV-cache cold-start surge. The autoscaler allowed scale-down that removed headroom faster than the allocator could rebuild cache during a short traffic burst, producing a queue backlog and request throttles.

Timeline (local times PST):
- 08:45: sudden increase in request concurrency and KV misses; queues begin to back up.
- 08:52: internal alerts triggered; 429s start increasing for ~2.5 minutes.
- 08:58: ops routed ~30% traffic to warm spare nodes and enabled smaller-model fallback.
- 09:05: queue depth reduced and latency returned to baseline.

Mitigations completed:
- Autoscaler hysteresis adjusted to prevent sub-minute scale-down for dedicated pools.
- Warm-standby policy updated: we will reserve an additional warm node for BrightRetail during your peak windows (configurable).
- Telemetry: created a BrightRetail dashboard with queue-depth and KV-miss alerts and a runbook for automatic emergency routing.
- Load replay: scheduled for Tue 2026-11-10 to validate the changes under controlled burst patterns.

Credit options (please pick one):
A) 15% credit on the impacted week’s Dedicated invoice (applied to November billing cycle).
B) Credit equal to 50% of the token overage specifically attributable to the incident window (we’ll calculate and share the token delta).

Next steps:
- We’ll run the replay and share results (target 2026-11-10).
- Final RCA document and permanent mitigation checklist by 2026-11-12.
- If you prefer a different credit structure, we can discuss.

Would you like that 30-minute technical walk-through this week or next? We can include Aditya and the allocator team.

Apologies again for the disruption — we’re treating this as high priority and will follow through on the operational improvements.

Best,

Kimberly Park
Account Lead, Enterprise Success
Redwood Inference
